stand: NATO's Baltic flank is hardening further. Lithuania is deploying troops to help guard its border with Kaliningrad after a Latvian border incident and fears of Russian mobilisation. Vilnius is pressing Washington for a permanent US base, courting Trump's non-committal interest, while roughly 1,000 US troops resume rotations in late October. Estonia is running NATO's biggest-ever command exercise, Steadfast Duel. Moscow calls NATO's new 'Theory of Victory' eastern-flank plan preparation for aggression and repeats its Kaliningrad weapons threat; NATO denies isolating the enclave. Poland and Lithuania plan for mass war refugees.

figures.label: Pabradė base capacity cited for a potential permanent base

claims.text: Putin warns Russia could deploy all its weapons in response to a direct attack on Russia, including Kaliningrad.
claims.by: Says: Vladimir Putin, at the Valdai Discussion Club.

claims.text: Russia accuses NATO of seeking to isolate or block Kaliningrad; NATO rejects the accusation.
claims.by: Says: Kremlin, in a formal diplomatic note to NATO. Denies: NATO, calling its regional activities defensive.

claims.text: Lithuania's parliament voted to remove the constitutional ban on nuclear weapons and foreign military bases; a second vote is required in January.
claims.by: Says: Seimas Speaker Juozas Olekas.

claims.text: The Kremlin says Russia will be forced to take retaliatory measures if nuclear weapons or a NATO base are deployed in Lithuania.
claims.by: Says: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov.

claims.text: Estonia has adopted an 'active defense' strategy, relocating its main brigade toward the Russian border and buying long-range strike weapons.
claims.by: Says: Estonian defence officials and military intelligence, cited by the Financial Times.

claims.text: The Kremlin downplays Estonia's troop shift, saying Russian intelligence already monitors border movements.
claims.by: Says: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov.  (brushes aside the FT report rather than denying it factually).

claims.text: Putin dismisses Estonian government statements about readiness to fight Russia as absurd.
claims.by: Says: Vladimir Putin.  — mocks rather than factually denies.

claims.text: Trump says the US will consider a permanent military base in Lithuania.
claims.by: Says: US President Donald Trump, responding to Lithuania's invitation.

claims.text: Lithuania has formally submitted a proposal for a permanent US base to the Pentagon; talks are under way and 'signals are positive'.
claims.by: Says: Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas.

claims.text: Poland and Lithuania tested cross-border evacuation for the first time during a Lithuanian national mobilisation exercise, with a 20-person Polish team taking part.
claims.by: Says: Lithuanian interior minister Martynas Katelynas and Polish counterpart Marcin Kierwiński.

claims.text: Germany's foreign intelligence chief warns Germany faces a real risk of low-intensity Russian military activity in the Baltic states.
claims.by: Says: BND chief Martin Jaeger.

claims.text: UK Royal Navy chief says the JEF offers partner states a 'nuclear umbrella'; an Estonian security expert says no separate guarantee is actually being offered.
claims.by: Says: First Sea Lord Gwyn Jenkins. Denies: security expert Meelis Oidsalu.

claims.text: Two US Army battalions are expected to arrive in Lithuania in late October.
claims.by: Says: Lithuanian Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas.

claims.text: Poland will deploy Patriot air-defence batteries near Lublin airport to protect airspace near the Ukrainian border, and form new drone units.
claims.by: Says: Polish Deputy PM and Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz.

claims.text: Lithuania is deploying its armed forces to help border guards protect the border with Russia's Kaliningrad region, as a preventive measure.
claims.by: Says: Interior Minister Martynas Katelynas.

claims.text: The deployment follows an incident on the Latvian border and reports that Russia could announce a mobilisation.
claims.by: Says: Interior Minister Martynas Katelynas.

claims.text: A group of at least 20 migrants, escorted by masked armed individuals, tried to cross from Belarus into Latvia; the group later sabotaged border infrastructure.
claims.by: Says: Latvia's National Armed Forces.

claims.text: A Russian Duma member calls NATO's new 'Theory of Victory' eastern-flank defence plan preparation for aggression against Russia and a lever to raise allied defence spending.
claims.by: Says: State Duma member and retired Maj. Gen. Leonid Ivlev.

claims.text: Trump also signals support for Poland's long-running push for a permanent US base.
claims.by: Says: US President Donald Trump.

claims.text: An Estonian-based defence researcher says Lithuania's current infrastructure could not host a full permanent US base, and the Pentagon leans toward cutting troop levels in Europe rather than adding bases.
claims.by: Says: Tomas Jermalavičius, International Centre for Defence and Security.

claims.text: A Russian court sentenced Igor Odintsov, a Kaliningrad man Lithuania had returned to Russia after an asylum request, to six years in prison over anti-war social media posts.
claims.by: Says: Baltic Fleet Military Court.

claims.text: Lithuania's return of Odintsov to Russia is called a betrayal by the Kaliningrad Lithuanian community; Lithuania's border guard says it was unclear he had made a formal asylum claim.
claims.by: Says: Sigitas Šamborskis, Lithuanian community in Kaliningrad. Denies: Lithuania's State Border Guard Service.

timeline.text: Igor Odintsov swims from Kaliningrad to Lithuania via the Nemunas, requests asylum, is returned to Russia the same day.
A Russian Mi-8 helicopter from Kaliningrad enters Polish airspace for about 42 seconds.
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte says there is no imminent threat to Alliance territory despite Russia's threats.
Russia's Baltic Fleet Military Court sentences Odintsov to six years in a penal colony.
Putin warns at the Valdai Discussion Club that an attack on Russia would put use of 'all weapons' on the agenda.
UK First Sea Lord's Baltic Sea comments, reported as touching on a 'nuclear umbrella' for JEF states, prompt debate in Estonia.
Financial Times reports Estonia is relocating its main brigade toward the Russian border under an 'active defense' strategy.
Kremlin's Peskov brushes aside the FT report on Estonia's troop shift, citing Russian intelligence capability.
Lithuania says infrastructure for the planned German brigade deployment remains on schedule.
Lithuanian and Polish interior ministers meet to discuss a joint evacuation plan for up to a million Baltic refugees.
Trump says he will consider a permanent US military base in Lithuania, responding to Lithuania's invitation.
Lithuania's Seimas votes 106-18 to lift the constitutional ban on nuclear weapons and foreign bases; a second vote is due 12 January.
Kremlin's Peskov says Russia will be forced to retaliate against nuclear weapons or a NATO base in Lithuania.
A NATO reconnaissance aircraft (Bombardier ARTEMIS II) is again seen circling the Kaliningrad Region.
Poland's defence minister announces Patriot batteries near Lublin and new drone units at the Ukrainian border.
Estonia's defence minister confirms loitering-munition drones are already deployed and the unit trained.
Masked, armed individuals push a migrant group toward the Latvian-Belarusian border, then sabotage a border electricity panel and steal CCTV cameras.
NATO's largest-ever command exercise, Steadfast Duel 26, begins with Estonia and all 32 member states, running to 15 Oct.
Lithuania orders its armed forces to help guard the border with Kaliningrad as a preventive measure.
Duma member Leonid Ivlev brands NATO's new 'Theory of Victory' eastern-flank plan preparation for aggression against Russia.
Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda welcomes Trump's base remark, urges Lithuania to act consistently while awaiting the troop rotation.
Estonia incorporates 'active defense' concept into national defence policy.

headline: Lithuania militarises Kaliningrad border as NATO drills and base talks intensify
